subject: Calibration: ratings alignment & org-change considerations
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Calibration: ratings alignment & org-change considerations

Team —

Ahead of next week's all-manager calibration session I put together an initial workbook with current proposed ratings and a couple of notes where I think cross-team context will matter (notably Platform eng vs. Product infra). See attached: performance_calibration_draft_v1.xlsx.

A few specific asks:
- Marcus: can you flag 3-4 ICs in Platform who might need cross-team adjustment because of scope changes?
- Grace: can you review the midline vs. high performer criteria in sheet #2 — we had slightly different buckets across teams last cycle.
- Monica: can you confirm what we can and cannot surface during calibration given pending org-change communications (I want to avoid creating leaks).

I also attached the calibration_guidelines.pdf — it's the HR-friendly rubric we agreed on last quarter. If we can close the draft by EOD Tuesday I’ll lock ratings for the review committee by Wednesday morning.

Thanks — appreciate quick reads here as this touches a few sensitive moves.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calibration: ratings alignment & org-change considerations

Thanks Lauren — downloaded the workbook and started a pass. Two quick notes:

1) Platform: there are three folks whose impact spans infra and product-owned systems; I flagged them in the "CrossTeam Flags" column and left a 1-paragraph rationale. I'm leaning toward keeping their ratings but adjusting stretch goals so that performance narratives reflect cross-team dependency.

2) Timeline: I can do a deeper sweep Mon afternoon and add suggested narrative bullets if that helps your lock deadline.

I'll also call out one person (E. Alvarez) who is in a formal performance plan — we should decide if that remains private to HR or discussed in the full calibration.

On the latter, Monica — what's your guidance? If we keep it private, can you annotate the workbook with a restricted flag?

—Marcus
Senior Engineering Manager
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calibration: ratings alignment & org-change considerations

Lauren, Marcus — I reviewed sheet #2 and left inline comments on rows where teams historically used different phrasing for "consistently meets" vs "strong contributor." I agree with Marcus on keeping ratings conservative for cross-team folks and focusing the narrative on collaboration metrics.

One more operational ask: can we run the committee with anonymized names for the first pass and then unmask? It helped reduce anchoring bias last cycle. Not sure where we stand on that from a tooling perspective.

—Grace
Group Manager, Data & Analytics
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calibration: ratings alignment & org-change considerations

Thanks for the heads-up. A couple of HR constraints to keep in mind:

- Individuals on an active PIP (performance improvement plan) should not be discussed in open, non-HR threads. Marcus, please remove E. Alvarez from the shared workbook and I'll create a private HR-only sheet.
- Regarding anonymization: we can provide the committee with an anonymized export (IDs only) but the committee lead must hold the key to remap names. That process worked last cycle and HR will produce the export if you confirm the list.
- Org-change comms: until the executive announcement is scheduled, please do not surface role/title transition speculation in narratives. If a rating change is driven by a role change, flag it in "Notes for Execs" and I will coordinate wording.

I'll create the private tab and a short changelog by EOD Monday. If you want, I can also join the calibration session for the first 15 minutes to ensure process adherence.

—Monica
People Operations Partner
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calibration: ratings alignment & org-change considerations

Appreciate the fast turnaround and clear guidance.

Actions:
- Marcus: remove E. Alvarez from the shared workbook and add a placeholder note; use the "CrossTeam Flags" column for the three Platform folks you called out.
- Grace: please prepare the anonymized list export (IDs only) — Monica will take it from there if we agree to anonymize first pass.
- Monica: yes, please add the private HR tab and join the first fifteen minutes — that'll help keep the conversation focused.

I'll lock the current workbook for editing at 9am PT Tuesday and will post the committee dial and anonymized export link by then. Thanks all — leaning into process here to avoid any accidental leaks while we finalize org updates next week.

—Lauren
Director, Product Management
